annotation.title_clean: امکان‌سنجی اعطای شخصیت حقوقی به ربات‌های هوشمند با تکیه بر مصوبه اتحادیه اروپا (شخص الکترونیک - 2017)
annotation.title_en: Feasibility Study of Granting Legal Personality to Smart Robots Based on the European Union Resolution (Electronic Person - 2017)
annotation.venue: Majlis and Rahbord (Parliament and Strategy Quarterly), Vol. 27, No. 103
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Persian peer-reviewed article from Iran's Parliament research journal assessing the feasibility of granting legal personality ("electronic person") to smart robots, based on the 2017 EU Parliament resolution. Using a descriptive-analytical method, it concludes that personhood is not currently feasible given robots' autonomy levels, but would face no obstacle if robots reached full autonomy, perception and will.
key_provisions_or_claims: Self-learning autonomous robots create a liability gap because victims struggle to attribute defects to manufacturer, owner or user.
The EU proposed electronic personhood to close the responsibility gap and protect victims.
Granting legal personality to smart robots is currently not feasible given their level of autonomy.
If robots attain full autonomy, perception and will, there would be no barrier to granting legal personality.
Robots are classified by autonomy level (weak, semi-autonomous, fully autonomous); cites Korea's Intelligent Robots Act definition.
